Content_Bio_Briefing:
Marcus Thorne, the city's most celebrated and controversial architect, has been found dead in his penthouse studio atop the unfinished 'Glass Tower'. His skull was crushed. The room is a fortress of glass and concrete, locked from the inside, with only a private elevator for access.

The initial sweep suggests a robbery gone wrong, as several items appear disturbed, but the brutality of the kill suggests passion. Thorne had many enemies: a scorned wife, an underpaid contractor, a terrified CFO, and a bitter rival. 

However, the devil is in the details. The studio is filled with high-tech fabrication equipment and servers. You need to look past the obvious red herrings and dig into the digital footprint of the building. Somewhere in the logs, the killer left a trace that physical cleaning couldn't wipe away.

Content_Bio_Briefing: A legal document prepared for signature. It explicitly states that all intellectual property regarding the 'Spire' project belongs solely to Marcus Thorne. Elias Vane is listed as 'Junior Assistant' with no equity.
Notes_Clues: Thorne claiming full credit for Spire|Vane's name removed
Description: Crisp legal document on bond paper.

Position: Intellectual Property Theft / Professional Jealousy. Thorne was stealing credit for Vane's masterpiece.
Rotation: The autopsy places death between 22:30 and 23:00. The Server Log (ENT_02) shows a file deletion at 23:15 using Thorne's credentials, implying the killer was in the room after death. The log identifies the source IP as 192.168.1.104. The Network Map (ENT_03) links this IP to Elias Vane's laptop. Vane's laptop (ENT_07) confirms the MAC address match. The weapon was a heavy 3D printed model (Blue PLA) of the Spire, indicated by the blue plastic in the wound (ENT_01). Vane melted the weapon in the kiln (ENT_04) to destroy the shape, but the material composition remains undeniable.
